name: Art Is Trash
headline: Art Is Trash – Ephemeral Street Art from Barcelona
bio: Art Is Trash is the street-art identity of Francisco de Pajaro, an artist closely connected with Barcelona's urban-art scene. His practice transforms discarded cardboard, furniture, rubbish bags and other abandoned materials into temporary characters and installations in public space.
seo_text:
Art Is Trash brings Barcelona’s urban environment directly into the creative process. Discarded cardboard, broken furniture, rubbish bags and other abandoned objects become temporary characters and spontaneous street interventions. The works are often humorous and expressive, but they also draw attention to waste, consumer culture and the materials that cities leave behind.

Because many interventions disappear when the streets are cleaned, photography and Instagram form an important visual record. The selected posts above document this temporary relationship between artwork, object and location. Francisco de Pájaro’s approach shows how street art can exist outside conventional walls and murals: the city itself supplies the materials, setting and audience. Within Barcelona’s independent urban-art scene, Art Is Trash represents an immediate form of creativity that is deliberately temporary, accessible and closely connected with everyday public space.

name: Ashwan
headline: Ashwan – Hip-Hop, Lettering and Contemporary Urban Art
bio: Ashwan is a Barcelona-based contemporary artist whose work connects hip-hop culture, graffiti influences, lettering and mixed media. His practice frequently transforms discarded cardboard and everyday materials into layered artworks that move between urban culture and contemporary art.
seo_text:
Ashwan’s work connects contemporary urban art with lettering, hip-hop culture and the creative reuse of everyday materials. Cardboard and other modest surfaces become spaces for layered compositions, rhythmic marks and graphic forms. This combination gives the work an informal street-level character while allowing it to move naturally between illustration, painting and mixed-media art.

The Instagram works selected above offer a compact view of Ashwan’s visual practice in Barcelona. Strong lines, written elements and improvised surfaces create a direct link with the city’s urban culture. Rather than separating studio art from street influences, the work allows both worlds to overlap. Ashwan’s profile on Urban Arts News forms part of the wider Barcelona collection, connecting the artist with other independent creators and with the city’s evolving visual language.

name: Si Beriana
headline: Si Beriana – Colorful Figurative Street Art in Barcelona
bio: Si Beriana creates colorful figurative street art and murals connected with Barcelona's contemporary urban-art scene. Her work combines expressive characters, strong outlines and vibrant color with the architecture and visual energy of public space.
seo_text:
Si Beriana’s work is characterised by vivid colour, expressive figures and a strong graphic presence. Her characters bring personality and movement to walls and urban surfaces, creating images that remain immediately recognisable within busy public environments. Bold outlines and energetic colour combinations give the work a direct visual impact.

The three selected Instagram posts above document different examples of this figurative approach. Together they show how character-based street art can interact with Barcelona’s architecture and everyday street life. Si Beriana’s work adds a colourful, human dimension to the city’s contemporary urban-art scene and demonstrates how murals can create encounters between an artist, a location and the people passing through it. This profile connects her selected works with the broader Urban Arts News archive of Barcelona artists.

name: Peeta
headline: Peeta – Sculpting Urban Space Through Optical Illusion
bio: Peeta, the artist name of Manuel Di Rita, is an Italian urban artist internationally known for three-dimensional lettering, geometric compositions and anamorphic murals. Active in graffiti since the early 1990s, his work has evolved from traditional lettering into a distinctive visual language combining painting, sculpture, architecture and optical illusion. Peeta often incorporates windows, corners and structural elements of buildings into his compositions, making walls appear to bend, expand or break apart. His work transforms architecture into an active part of the artwork and represents a striking evolution of contemporary graffiti and urban art.
seo_text:
Peeta transforms architectural surfaces through geometry, three-dimensional lettering and optical illusion. His compositions appear to bend walls, extend corners and open new spaces inside existing buildings. Windows, edges and structural details are often incorporated into the artwork, making architecture an active part of the final image rather than a neutral background.

The selected Instagram posts above demonstrate the precision and spatial imagination associated with his work. Shapes seem to project beyond the wall or recede into it, changing how viewers perceive scale, depth and structure. This distinctive combination of graffiti, anamorphic art and contemporary mural painting has made Peeta an important reference within Italian urban art. His profile connects Venice with the wider international development of three-dimensional street art and architectural intervention.

name: Spogo
headline: Spogo – Contemporary Urban Art from Badalona
bio: Spogo is an urban artist connected with Badalona, Spain. Urban Arts News presents selected works from the artist's public Instagram archive as part of its city-based documentation of contemporary street art, visual culture and independent urban creativity.
seo_text:
Spogo’s selected works reveal an abstract approach to urban art built around colour, geometry, rhythm and carefully balanced forms. Rather than relying on conventional characters or lettering, the compositions create movement through overlapping shapes, lines and contrasting areas of colour. Walls become large visual fields that interact with the surrounding architecture.

The three Instagram posts above provide a focused introduction to Spogo’s work and its connection with Badalona. Each piece demonstrates how abstraction can change the atmosphere of a public surface without separating the artwork from its location. The relationship between mural, building and neighbourhood is central to the viewing experience. By documenting Spogo within the Badalona collection, Urban Arts News expands its coverage beyond central Barcelona and highlights the wider metropolitan area as an active space for contemporary urban creativity.
